correctness.rationale: Over any commutative k-algebra R, the Frobenius relations on generator images separate coefficient by coefficient because distinct surviving monomials stay distinct after scaling by p^{a_i}. Exactly u_i coefficients of image i (including its constant term) are constrained by their p^{a_i}-th powers. For each residue field the constant terms vanish, and invertible cotangent action implies surjectivity on each graded piece of the maximal-ideal filtration and hence invertibility. On the full finite free R-module this criterion holds exactly when all residue-field fibers are invertible, by the determinant criterion; it does not require assuming every substitution preserves the augmentation over nonreduced R. Modulo a nilpotent ideal of constrained coefficients the linear matrix is block triangular, with blocks ordered by exponent value. Inverting its determinant is equivalent to inverting the product of the block determinants since the difference is nilpotent. This gives the proposed scheme product, not a law of composition. Its nilradical is the truncated-coordinate ideal; the ordinary-variable quotient is geometrically reduced and connected. The monomial basis in the truncated coordinates gives the exact free rank, while all defining power equations have zero first differentials, giving tangent dimension dN. Every u_i is positive, so tangent dimension always exceeds local dimension. Over a field the constrained coordinates have only value zero, leaving precisely the stated point-count formula.
residual_risks: The direct count is one bounded finite example; finite-field points cannot check nilpotent structure. The proof treats all commutative k-algebras for fixed k, with no claim that the displayed factors multiply independently as groups.

evidence: Chang–Shu–Yao's finite-level determinant criterion is for a field and common p-power height. Ma's relevant identification is height one, and the arbitrary divided-power-height discussion is about a different algebraic structure.

evidence: An abelian restricted p-Lie chain of length a_i per variable presents the same associative algebra via its restricted enveloping algebra. The same ring is also the additive Hopf coordinate algebra of a product of alpha_{p^{a_i}}.

Restricted-Lie and Hopf automorphisms must preserve extra structure; for instance Hopf automorphisms of alpha_p^d just act by invertible linear maps on the primitives, while plain algebra automorphisms admit higher terms and infinitesimal translations. Ma identifies the ordinary height-one coordinate scheme with the W(n;1) automorphism scheme under its stated characteristic and base assumptions.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The ordinary algebra functor is not equivalent to classifying structured automorphisms of the associated group scheme or restricted-Lie presentation, and the height-one Witt correspondence does not give arbitrary mixed heights.

value.rationale: The arbitrary mixed-height decomposition separates rational symmetry from infinitesimal symmetry: e.g. it specifies the lengths of each nonreduced coordinate, which are invisible to the rational counts and are not determined by counting tangent directions. It gives a uniform usable coordinate presentation for nonreduced base changes and a simultaneous counting formula for a standard family of local complete intersections. The value survives crediting the exact small and equal-height cases.
residual_risks: No claim that this classifies the group law or that this pattern extends to arbitrary monomial ideals.
